image_description: A close-up, vertical shot of a grey whale's head emerging vertically from deep blue water. The rostrum is arched and covered in distinctive white barnacle patches (callosities) against dark grey skin. Water splashes around the base of the emergence. No body, flippers, or tail are visible due to the tight framing.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows the characteristic arched rostrum of a grey whale. While the blowholes are at the very top edge and partially obscured by splash/lighting, the overall head shape and arch are distinct and match the species description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture is highly detailed, showing the rough, mottled grey surface with significant white encrustations (barnacles/cyamids) typical of grey whales, particularly on the rostrum.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image only captures the head and immediate neck area emerging from the water. The posterior back where dorsal knuckles would be located is completely outside the frame/submerged.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the head is visible. The full body shape cannot be verified from this crop.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the Head_and_Face checkpoint, the visible skin exhibits the correct mottling and barnacle coverage.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed or not visible from this angle; baleen plates are internal/under the upper jaw and not exposed in this view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located further down the body and are submerged/out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Tail is completely out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The high-resolution detail on the head confirms the rough, bumpy texture associated with callosities and barnacles.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The water ripples have a slightly repetitive, 'painted' quality rather than natural fluid dynamics. Some splash droplets appear fused or lack individual definition, suggesting minor generative smoothing.

artifact_observations.location: Interface between whale head and water line
artifact_observations.reasoning: Slight softness/blurring at the contact point where the whale emerges from the water. The transition isn't perfectly sharp, with some grey tones bleeding into the blue water, typical of AI generation struggles with complex wet interfaces.

To rigorously assess the subtle texture anomalies in the water and splash physics which are common failure points in AI marine imagery.
To check for structural continuity of the head and ensure no melting artifacts occur at the high-contrast boundary between the dark skin and bright barnacles.

Structural integrity of the rostrum arch
Realism of water displacement and splash physics
Edge sharpness at the water-line interface
